claims.text: AlCoFeNi and AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi are magnetic high-entropy alloy systems.
Introducing a hierarchically decomposed B2 + A2 structure can increase the coercive field.
The relevant hierarchical structure consists of A2 precipitates in a B2 matrix.
Magnetic vortices occur within A2 precipitates.
Successive reversal of magnetic vortices within A2 precipitates contributes to coercivity.
Interactions between the A2-precipitate vortices and a weakly ferromagnetic B2 matrix contribute to the increased coercive field.
Annealing at 600°C for 15 hours in argon followed by water quenching is the processing condition under which the proposed effect should hold.
The hierarchically decomposed alloy should have a higher coercive field than the stated AlCoFeNi baseline.
The AlCoFeNi baseline lacks a hierarchically decomposed B2 + A2 structure.
Interactions among the different magnetic elements are unclear.
Further experiments are needed to determine how external magnetic fields or stress annealing affect precipitate formation.
The effects of temperature, strain, and magnetic field on precipitate formation remain uncertain.
The proposed experiment will compare coercive fields and magnetization curves for alloys with and without the hierarchical B2 + A2 structure.
Failure of AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi to exhibit a significantly higher coercive field than AlCoFeNi would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention is defined as introducing the hierarchical structure, and the design proposes with-versus-without-structure comparisons, but the falsification rule instead compares two different alloy compositions. This does not isolate the stated structural intervention and is not a composition-matched baseline.
